title: Unit 3: RAG, Embeddings & SQL Conversation Logs

lessons.title: 3. Storing AI Conversations & RAG Context in SQL
lessons.description: RAG evaluation starts by logging conversations as structured rows (later stored in a table). Implement format_conversation_log(user_id, prompt, response) returning a dict with keys 'user_id', 'prompt', 'response' and a cheap 'tokens' estimate: len(prompt.split()) + len(response.split()). Tests check the user id and that tokens > 0 for a real exchange.

tests.name: test_conversation_log
tests.unittest_code:
def test_conversation_log(self):
    log = format_conversation_log(1, 'Hello AI', 'Hello Human')
    self.assertEqual(log['user_id'], 1)
    self.assertGreater(log['tokens'], 0)

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — Mapping Types — building logging rows as dicts

learning_objectives: Shape conversation logs as dict rows ready for a database insert
Estimate token counts with a whitespace heuristic
Understand that RAG evaluation needs stored prompts and outputs
